observations.description: The decoded value for IEC104 IOA 1007 changed by approximately 48.3 between frames 10 and 11, following a change of approximately 0.9 between frames 9 and 10. The value then changed only approximately 0.6 by frame 12. This is a temporal anomaly in the supplied series, not confirmation of an attack.
possible_explanations: A legitimate step change in the underlying physical process
A sensor, transducer, scaling, or acquisition-system transition
A transient data-quality or decoding issue not represented by the available fields
Unauthorized alteration of the measurement, which cannot be established from these frames alone
recommended_checks: Compare the IOA 1007 values with the underlying process records and independent sensors around frame 11
Review device and gateway logs for configuration, restart, calibration, or input-channel changes
Inspect additional IEC104 traffic before frame 9 and after frame 12 for persistence or reversion of the change
observations.title: Abrupt measurement transition at frame 11

observations.description: Across frames 9–12, the measurement fields show quality 0, negative false, test false, and cause of transmission 3. These stable decoded fields provide no protocol-level indication in the supplied evidence that the abrupt value change was marked as invalid, test data, or a changed transmission cause.
possible_explanations: The source reported the transition as ordinary valid process data
The protocol quality indicators do not encode the type of underlying sensor or application fault
A data-source or application-layer problem could occur without changing these fields
recommended_checks: Verify how quality value 0 is defined and populated by the originating endpoint
Check device diagnostics and raw sensor status for the interval containing frame 11
Correlate with redundant measurements or application alarms
observations.title: Measurement quality and cause fields remain unchanged

observations.description: Frames 9–12 contain sequential transmitted APCI values tx 2, 3, 4, and 5, while rx remains 1. The supplied state series reports three observed tx changes and no rx changes, with no reordered events or retransmissions. This supports continuity of the observed protocol stream but does not validate the physical correctness of the measurement.
possible_explanations: The endpoint transmitted four consecutive information frames normally
The capture may represent only a partial session and may not show all acknowledgements or traffic
A correctly sequenced protocol stream can still carry erroneous, stale, or manipulated application data
recommended_checks: Review the complete bidirectional IEC104 session, including acknowledgements and supervisory frames
Confirm endpoint identity, connection state, and expected sequence-number behavior
Compare the application values with source-device logs rather than relying only on APCI continuity
observations.title: Consistent IEC104 sequencing in the observed exchange

observations.description: Measurements were observed at relative times 1000, 2000, 3000, and 4000 ms, with zero interval standard deviation and no nonpositive time differences in the supplied statistics. The abrupt value transition therefore occurred between consecutive regularly spaced observations rather than during an apparent timing irregularity.
possible_explanations: The source uses a regular periodic reporting schedule
A process change occurred between the regularly scheduled reports
The capture or preprocessing may omit events outside the supplied frame range
recommended_checks: Inspect packet timestamps and reporting configuration over a longer interval
Determine whether the source reports cyclic values or event-triggered values on this connection
Check for unsampled changes or related object updates between the supplied frames
observations.title: Regular one-second observation interval

result.summary: IEC104 measurements for IOA 1007 increased gradually from approximately 101.2 to 102.1, then changed abruptly to approximately 150.4 and 151.0 across frames 9–12. Protocol sequencing and quality-related fields remained consistent, and the available evidence does not establish whether the change reflects a physical process event, a measurement-source issue, or malicious activity.
